validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's current ref (KNOE, Jul 2019) headlines a '252-mile pipeline' from 'near Port Arthur, Texas, to Delhi, Louisiana' -- that figure describes the whole announced corridor/system in an early press writeup, not the specific FERC-defined 'Louisiana Connector Extension Project' facility. TWO independent primary sources -- the FERC Docket PF19-6-000 Notice of Intent to prepare an EIS (federalregister.gov, 84 FR 48133, 2019-09-12) and Port Arthur Pipeline/Sempra LNG's own project page (sempralng.com, Wayback 2021-05-11) -- both state the Extension itself is 'approximately 166 miles' of new 48-inch pipe confined to Allen, Evangeline, Rapides, Grant, La Salle, Catahoula, Franklin and Richland Parishes, Louisiana (the separate widening of the already-approved base Louisiana Connector from 42in to 48in between mileposts 0-86, spanning into Jefferson County TX and Cameron/Calcasieu/Beauregard/Allen Parishes LA, is a distinct scope item on the BASE connector, not new Extension pipe -- and that base connector is a different GEM row, P0241, in batch A3). Diameter (48in) and Capacity (2.5 Bcfd = 2,500 MMcf/d) both check out against the recorded/blank values. Length is the one material disagreement: 252 (recorded, sourced only to a rounded press estimate) vs 166 (two independent primary/operator-disclosed sources, in exact agreement with each other).

cross_row_leads.facts: Sempra Infrastructure's base Port Arthur Pipeline Louisiana Connector (the already-approved CP18-7-000 project, ~72-131 mi of 42-inch pipe depending on source, Beauregard Parish compressor station) reached mechanical completion Jan 2026 and was placed IN-SERVICE 2026-06-09, delivered ahead of schedule and under budget, capex <$1B -- a major status change worth checking against P0241's own current sheet status (proposed/construction) in batch A3.

The FERC PF19-6-000 notice describes 'a new header system pipeline totaling 15 miles in length with various diameters' as part of the (never-formally-filed) Extension proposal -- length matches P3197's roster figure (15.0 mi) almost exactly, though P3197 (the actual 'Louisiana Connector Pipeline Amendment', Docket CP23-513-000, filed 2023-07-14, 38 modifications to the base connector's alignment/footprint/installation methods, EA noticed 2024-02-08) is a separate, later, formally-filed project -- worth checking whether P3197's 15-mile header figure derives from this same abandoned 2019 header-system concept or is independently sourced to the 2023 CP23-513 filing.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No independent news of revival, a formal CP application, or any progress since the FERC PF19-6-000 pre-filing docket opened 2019-06-21. The most recent primary evidence of the project's own status is Port Arthur Pipeline/Sempra's project page as archived 2021-05-11, which still described it as active/proposed (targeting Q2 2021 construction start, Q2 2024 commercial operation, and an application 'expected...in February 2020' that never materialized). Nothing dated after 2021 was found addressing this specific project -- FERC/Federal Register activity in 2023-2024 concerns the DIFFERENT Louisiana Connector Pipeline Amendment (CP23-513-000 = GEM P3197), not the Extension, and the base Louisiana Connector (P0241) reached in-service in mid-2026 without any indication the Extension revived alongside it. ShelvedYear on the sheet reads 2021; applying the sweep's 4-year shelved-to-cancelled dormancy rule against that date crosses the threshold in 2025, well before this 2026-09-10 review. Per standing rule 2, no fabricated ref is attached to this inferred status change; the sheet's existing but unsupported CancelledYear=2023 is addressed separately in validity (I could not source 2023 specifically, but the broader inference that the project has lapsed is sound). If GEM prefers to keep 'shelved' pending a documented cancellation, at minimum the unsupported CancelledYear=2023 should be cleared or replaced with this inferred 2025 date.

summary: P3590 Port Arthur Louisiana Connector Extension: real, well-documented FERC pre-filing project (PF19-6-000, 2019) that stalled after pre-filing and never received a CP application -- confirmed (caveat), 3 spec concerns staged (Length 252->166mi corrected via 2 independent primary sources; unsupported CancelledYear=2023 and StartYear1=2023 flagged), status review verdict=stale recommending Status->cancelled (inferred, dormancy >4y). All 18 worklist units carry a record; UNRESOLVED: Status, Construction, Start, Shelved, Cancelled, Pressure, FuelSource, SegmentCost (each searched and noted; project never reached construction/certification so several are genuinely unanswerable).
